text:
amanda: Hey folks — quick sync about error ergonomics for SDKs. We need a minimal typed-exception surface that's consistent across languages, gives actionable messages in the sample apps, and maps cleanly from HTTP codes -> retry semantics. Example current payload we ship in hosted API: ```json\n{"error": {"code":"rate_limit","message":"Too many requests","meta":{"retry_after":10}}}``` Is that enough?
jason: I like the meta field idea but we should standardize keys: `code`, `message`, `status`, `retry_hint` (string) and `retry_after` (seconds). Different SDKs can map into typed classes.
priya: +1 to typed classes. For onboarding sample apps we should avoid cryptic `code` values. Use namespaced, human-friendly values like `rate_limit.exceeded` or `auth.token_expired`. That helps UX copy in the sample UI.
lucas: Important: HTTP 429 -> non-fatal retryable; 5xx -> exponential backoff; 4xx (400,401,403) -> do not retry unless `retry_hint` says otherwise. We should include an explicit `retryable: true|false` boolean so SDKs don't infer incorrectly.
emily: Could be useful to include a short `user_message` separate from internal `message` so sample apps show something helpful without leaking internal details. Eg: `message`: "token signature invalid at verifier step 2", `user_message`: "Please sign in again."
amanda: Nice. So proposed canonical error shape: ```json\n{\n  "error": {\n    "code": "auth.token_expired",\n    "status": 401,\n    "message": "internal token expiry detail...",\n    "user_message": "Your session expired, please sign in.",\n    "retryable": false,\n    "retry_after": null,\n    "retry_hint": "refresh_token",\n    "meta": {"docs_url": "https://redwood.ai/errors#auth.token_expired"}\n  }\n}```
priya: Love that. SDKs can surface a typed `AuthTokenExpired` exception with fields `user_message`, `retry_hint`, and `docs_url`. Onboarding sample app can show `user_message` as the banner and optionally a CTA to refresh.
jason: One catch: some clients want minimal payload due to bandwidth/telemetry costs on mobile. We should support a compact mode (production) and verbose (debug). Maybe header `X-Error-Detail: verbose|compact`.
lucas: Agree. Also we need to document mapping rules: `status 429` -> `retryable=true` unless `retryable=false` explicitly set. `status 503` -> `retryable=true`. `status 401` -> `retryable=false` unless `retry_hint` present. Put these in docs and the SDK tests.
emily: For SDK parity, we should add a shared test harness: sample requests that assert typed exceptions, `retryable` bits, and `user_message` selection. That will catch language SDK divergence early.
amanda: Action items: 1) PR to API team to add `retryable`, `user_message`, and `retry_hint` fields to canonical error contract (priory: high). 2) DevEx to add sample app wiring to surface `user_message` and map `retry_hint` to CTA. 3) SDKs to implement typed exceptions and a compact/verbose toggle.
priya: I'll draft the API PR today and add the docs examples. Will ping @jason for review.
jason: I'll review; also add tests for HTTP -> retry mapping.
amanda: Thanks. Also small UX ask: make error messages in sample apps show a one-line summary and a collapsible details section that prints the `message` only in verbose debug mode. Keeps onboarding less scary.
emily: :thumbsup: I'll update the sample app UI.
ci-bot: build status: sample-apps/test-suite — failed on `sdk-go` error-shape test. https://ci.redwood.internal/1234
lucas: @ci-bot thanks — that failing test might be because go SDK hasn't implemented `retryable` parsing yet. I'll take it.
amanda: Perfect. Keep the thread updated if you hit any ambiguity in the API shape. Let's aim to land the api change + one SDK implementation in 2 sprints. :rocket:
